'''Lan Barell''' was a dusty, dry neutral backwater [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located on the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] near [[Breshkall]]. Heavy iron content in the soil gave the planet a faint blue sheen, and when combined with the red glare of its [[Star/Legends|sun]], gave the planet a garish and gloomy atmosphere.

==Description==
Lan Barell was the fourth [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of the [[Lan system]], located in the [[Hook Nebula/Legends|Hook Nebula]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. A dusty, hot, and dry terrestrial world, the moisture in the planet's atmosphere was locked in thin polar ice caps. Ore-rich, the heavy [[Iron/Legends|iron]] content in the planet's soil gave Lan Barell a faint blue sheen. The planet had standard [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] and a breathable Type I [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]]. A [[Standard day/Legends|day]] lasted twenty-three [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]], and a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] was comprised of 255 local days.<ref name="LB" />

The most inhabitable parts of Lan Barell were located on large plateaus that served as continents, while the uninhabitable wastelands known as the [[Lowlands (Lan Barell)|Lowlands]] separated the plateaus like oceans. At some point, Lan Barell possessed three [[Moon/Legends|moons]]. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], only two remained as the third had been stripped mined, broken down and refined. The remnants of the moon served as bases for [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] ore refining plants. The other two moons were scarred by strip mining.<ref name="LB" />

Lan Barell was the [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] of the [[Qieg/Legends|Qieg]], a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Insectoid/Legends|insectoids]]. Mechanically minded, the Qieg lived in colony nests throughout the [[cacti forests]] that covered the habitable plateaus. Lan Barell's main exports were [[Ore/Legends|ore]], minerals and other raw materials, which were then sold to [[Core Worlds/Legends|Coreward]]-bound [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]] and to systems in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]].<ref name="LB" />

[[Shulell City]] served as the planet's [[Capital/Legends|capital]], and the planetary government, the [[Human-Qieg Guild]], was based in the [[City/Legends|city]]. A [[Lan Barell space navy|space navy]] of one hundred vessels provided security for the system.<ref name="LB" />

==History==
The remote [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of Lan Barell was discovered by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] around [[1300 BBY/Legends|1300 BBY]], who discovered that the inner planets of the system were extremely rich in ore. Soon after discovery, [[Gaminne Group, Inc.]], a conglomerate looking to expand its mining operations, negotiated the rights to mine the inner planets from the Qieg. Under the agreement, a charter allowed [[Human/Legends|Human]] colonists to settle on Lan Barell and establish [[Shulell City]].<ref name="LB" />

Over the centuries, the original charter was lost to memory, and Gammine Group, Inc. ceased to exist. By the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], the Qieg and Human cultures considered the planet to be jointly owned. Despite Gammine Group, Inc.'s cessation, mining operations in the system continued, taken over by various companies. In turn, these companies formed the [[Human-Qieg Guild]], a conglomeration that was established to oversee the mines that became the government for the system.<ref name="LB" />

Over the years, the Human-Qieg Guild attempted to diversify their exports and attract new settlers, but such efforts ultimately failed. As a rule, more people left Lan Barell than arrived, which contributed to a low Human population.<ref name="LB" />

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] came to power<ref name="LB" /> in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Lan Barell became a haven for fringers and exiles. Being isolated and possessing a lax legal system, those beings wishing to avoid the Empire started to visit Lan Barell to offload smuggled goods, refugees and exiles.<ref name="LB" />

Around [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]], the Empire finally arrived to Lan Barell in the name of the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]. The visit was brief, amounting to little more than a show of force and receiving the [[oaths of fealty]] from the Human-Qieg Guild. The mining operations were valued for taxation purposes, while allwing the Guild to retain some self-government, with the Empire opening an [[Imperial Embassy (Lan Barell)|embassy]] in Shulell City which was staffed by four [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]] who had displeased their superiors. The Empire also collected taxes from Lan Barell mines. Twice a year, representatives of the nearby local [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] would arrive to remind the population of who was really in control.<ref name="LB" />

The [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Chyakk clan/Legends|Chyakk clan]] worked out of the [[Shulell City spaceport]], located twenty [[Meter/Legends|kilometers]] from the city of [[Carmelle]]. Under Imperial control, Lan Barell's legal system suffered from poor enforcement and several less-savory mining companies opened their doors on the world. As the Empire began to strengthen its hold on the planet in [[15 BBY/Legends|15 BBY]], the Empire allowed the Human-Qieg Guild to remain intact so long as they collected taxation for the Empire. Throughout Imperial control of the galaxy, many refugees fled to Lan Barell to hide in the mines of the planet in fear of persecution by the Empire.<ref name="LB" />

==Locations==
Shulell City was the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of Lan Barell. A Human-style settlement, it was inhabited by both Humans and Qieg. All financial transactions regarding the sale of ore and materials had to be processed and authorized at the city's center of commerce, the [[Quilan Hive]].<ref name="LB" />

The Lowlands, while being largely uninhabitable, were the location of a network of major mines on Lan Barell that had not yet been tapped out. Material from the mines was shipped via [[sub-orbital freighter]] to Shulell City for processing and refinement.<ref name="LB" />

The plateaus were home to a number of ranches that raised [[Dingory]], the primary meat source for both Humans and Qieg.<ref name="LB" />

==Inhabitants==
The cultures of the native Qieg and the long-time Human population merged into a single culture by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and the two races were partners in the governing of the planet. Each community saw the planet as jointly owned with the other. Qieg who interacted with Humans on a regular basis wore special masks that translated their speech and mandible movements into [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|basic]]. In turn, the Lan Barell humans learned to show emotion through hand gestures rather than facial expressions to mimic the way Qieq used their antenna.<ref name="LB" />
